the alpha 2 adrenerigic system is tonically active in the Zucker obese rat, and the beta 2 and beta 3 adrenergic systems are tonically less active in the same rat.
in the fatty Zucker rat the alpha 2 adrenergy system is tonically overactive, the beta 3 adrenergy system underactive and the beta 2 adrenegy system normal.
in the obese Zucker rat, alpha 2-adrenergic receptor activity is increased and beta 3-adrenergic receptors are decreased.

the role of the autonomic nervous system in the control of food intake.
the development of obesity, in particular in the Zucker fatty rat.
the role of central adrenergic systems in the control of food intake.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the beta 2 and beta 3 adrenergic systems are tonically less active in the fatty Zucker rat, and that the alpha 2 system is tonically hyperactive in these animals.
in obese Zucker rats, the beta 3-adrenergic system is tonically downregulated and that alpha 2-adrenergic activity is upregulated.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the obese Zucker rat is characterized by a hyperactive alpha 2 adrenerigic system, and a hypoactive beta 3 system.
in Zucker fatty rats, the alpha 1 receptor system is tonally active, and the alpha 2 system tonically less so.
the hyperphagic response of the fatty rat to alpha 2 receptor stimulation is blunted, and the response to beta 3 receptor stimulation enhanced.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the beta 3 adrenergic receptor system may play a role in the regulation of body weight in obese Zucker rats, but not lean rats.
we have developed a new class of drugs that have the ability to reduce food intake and increase energy expenditure, and that this is mediated by the beta 3 receptors.
the alpha 2 and beta 3 receptor systems are important in the control of feeding in the Zucker rat.
